T: Every time a bell rings, dessert's ready.
D: On Christmas Eve, a small-town man at the end of his rope is shown what Bedford Falls would be like without him.
P: Serve the chicken when George and Mary's honeymoon dinner turns on the record player.
S: George and Mary's bread, salt and wine for the Martinis' new house

Thick, airy focaccia dimpled with olive oil, rosemary and flaky salt, baked golden and served warm with good olive oil and balsamic for dipping. Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 10g salt and 400ml warm water into a wet dough. Cover and rest 2 hours, folding it over itself twice. Pour 4 tbsp olive oil into a 23 x 33cm tin, tip in the dough and stretch to the corners. Rest 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 220C. Dimple deeply with oiled fingers, drizzle with more oil, scatter rosemary and flaky salt and bake 25 minutes. Serve warm with oil and balsamic.
coconuts from Tahiti, young George's big dream
Desiccated coconut mixed with condensed milk, egg white and vanilla, scooped into mounds and baked at 160C until golden on the edges.
Puff pastry layered with sharp cheddar, parmesan and a pinch of cayenne, twisted into straws and baked crisp.
M: roasted on a spit turned by the record player
Whole chicken rubbed with butter, garlic and thyme, roasted at 200C until the skin crackles, with roast potatoes.
Sunday dinner at the Bailey house in Bedford Falls

Beef chuck browned and braised for hours with onions, carrots and potatoes in red wine and stock until it falls apart, with thick gravy. Heat the oven to 160C. Season 1.5kg beef chuck and brown well in oil in a casserole. Remove. Fry 2 onions in wedges for 5 minutes, add 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 tbsp flour, then 200ml red wine and 600ml beef stock, thyme and bay. Return the beef, cover and cook 2 hours. Add 4 carrots and 800g potatoes in chunks and cook 1 hour more. Simmer the liquid on the stove to thicken into gravy.
W: Mary at the soda fountain, no coconut thanks
Chocolate ice cream in tall glasses with hot fudge sauce, whipped cream and a cherry, served at the drugstore counter.
K: Milk and cream warmed with egg yolks, sugar, nutmeg and vanilla until thickened, served cold with more nutmeg on top.

s.note: coconuts from Tahiti, young George's big dream
s.how: Mix 250g desiccated coconut with 395g condensed milk, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt. Whisk 2 egg whites to stiff peaks and fold through. Scoop 20 mounds onto lined trays and bake at 160C for 20 minutes until golden on the edges.

Sprinkle 1 sheet puff pastry with 80g grated sharp cheddar, 30g parmesan and a pinch of cayenne, top with a second sheet and press. Cut into 2cm strips, twist each one and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp.

m.note: roasted on a spit turned by the record player
m.how: Rub a 1.8kg whole chicken with 50g soft butter mixed with 2 crushed garlic cloves, thyme leaves and salt. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes on a rack over 1kg potatoes in chunks, turning the potatoes halfway, until the juices run clear. Rest 10 minutes and carve.

w.note: Mary at the soda fountain, no coconut thanks
w.how: Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream into a hot fudge sauce. Scoop 1L chocolate ice cream into 4 tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with 200ml whipped cream and a maraschino cherry. No coconut.

d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 80g sugar. Heat 500ml milk and 250ml cream until steaming, whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon. Add 1 tsp vanilla, chill 3 hours and serve with grated nutmeg.
